method: All ten actual PNGs across batch27/28 independently viewed in groups of at most two. Complete manifests, current RAT/KOR/FOR space cards and screenplay scene setup/basis passages checked. Original 95/96 pixels not re-viewed; revisions assessed on their own pixels against stated targets and prior QA. No art, manifest, story or code changes.

limitations: Review concepts only; no native-grid, collision, engineering, animation, game or physical-safety validation.
Static objects never prove payments, rescue outcomes, consent, arrival, genealogy, authentic history or exact inventory.
No original reference images independently viewed in this pass; their byte hashes verified only.

findings.finding: Two closed lockers, two separate visibly different keys and blank plates appear behind a public retrieval window; this is not a display of all courtyard inventory. The one-night room has a closed letter, lamp, separate tally tray and closed bundle, with its own open front. The adjacent closed door and solid wall do not obstruct the public return; no bed is visible. Generic tally marks cannot communicate one-night versus monthly terms alone. Absence never becomes arrival, consent, actual lodging or renewed rent.

Two neighboring open domestic doorways under common eaves face separate walled courtyards, each with an open public-lane gate. Distinct circular/triangular markers support separate occupancy; rope-linked proxy-tag semantics are not unambiguous. The small dwelling has its own open side/front corner door to the public lane, closed bag, plain cup/box and blank removable board. Its visible steps are not a no-step specification violation here, but accessibility and collision need design. No selected home, blood relationship, inherited identity or proxy permission can be inferred.

Exactly one framed painting is shown from its wooden back on one easel, with no face or official identity supplied. Opposite table has three separate square/circular/triangular tokens in three trays, three closed folios and three short benches. Both spaces approach the open public yard independently. Backboard damage/mark is only a visual cue, not authenticated age or authorship. Separate tokens do not enact consent for belongings, lodging or representation.

Return hatch shows an uncrested bundle and a notched claim-token shape; detached blank nameboard does not block the open side gate and visible route beyond. Separate eave has exactly one empty long bench and a public arrow sign. Fee shelf has blank slate, lamp and a STACKED CYLINDRICAL token-like prop rather than one unmistakable notched wooden oil tally. Refine its silhouette to avoid currency/count ambiguity. Source card describes a settled one-night tally, but blank static props alone cannot establish settlement, actual handoff, arrival or authorized monthly rent.

Left compartment of the right accounting table visibly holds five elongated rectangular brown wooden sticks, clearly distinct from metallic coins. Notches are too subtle for reliable gameplay reading and need final-sprite refinement. Two closed pouches remain in separate compartments; two ore scales and front exit routes remain visible. Prefer v2 for non-currency share representation. Five drawn sticks are not a defined share quantity, rights allocation, wage amount or completed payment. Original pixels were not independently re-viewed in this pass, so no pixel-exact preservation claim is made.

overall: KOR public retrieval, separate sleeping privacy and independent exits supported; 109 exact one/three composition passes. 96 v2 mine shares read as wood rather than money. 110 oil tally silhouette needs refinement.
